newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MARIO LEMIEUX TO PLAY IN 1996-97, PENGUINS SAY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MARIO LEMIEUX TO PLAY IN 1996-97, PENGUINS SAY.

text.p: Pittsburgh Penguins superstar centre Mario Lemieux will be back for the upcoming 1996-97 National Hockey League season, the team announced on Monday.
Penguins owner Howard Baldwin announced Lemieux's intent to return for this season at the team's training facility. Lemieux was not available to comment on the announcement.

Lemieux, who captured his third Hart Memorial Trophy as the league's Most Valuable Player last season, opted not to play for Canada in the World Cup and had been undecided about fulfilling the final year of his current contract.
The 31-year-old centre amazed the hockey world by leading the league in scoring last season after taking a year off to recover from treatment for Hodgkins disease and back surgery.
He captured his fifth scoring title with 161 points, leading the league in goals with 69 and assists with 92.
He was also tops in the league with 31 powerplay goals and eight short-handed tallies.
